venture.description: A rugged, solar-powered, rechargeable flashlight, lantern, and cell phone charger.
venture.note: Designed for power outages and rugged conditions.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy introduces herself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene introduces himself and the name of their product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy states their ask of one hundred fifty thousand dollars for ten percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene describes the problem of power going out at home or while camping.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy transitions to demonstrating the product by breaking a block of ice.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene smashes the ice with a bat to reveal the working device inside.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene explains the device is super tough, solar-powered, rechargeable, and has three functions.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy states that their device is much more than just another solar flashlight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene highlights its three-year charge hold, forty-eight hours of light, and floating ability.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy mentions they donate at least twenty-five percent of profits to global partners.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene expresses their vision to see the device in every home, workplace, and campsite.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy concludes the pitch by asking who wants to partner with them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how to turn the device on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene demonstrates the button to turn on the flashlight and the room lantern.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori acknowledges the demonstration.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene explains how to activate the table lantern mode.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert shows the device being used as a reading lantern.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene points out the green lights that indicate battery level.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks about the solar charging time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene states it takes twenty-two hours to charge via solar.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy adds that it can be charged with electricity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks how long an electrical charge takes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy says it takes one hour.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy explains it can also charge a cell phone via a USB cable.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark makes playful alien noises with the light.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene reacts to Mark's joke.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin holds the light under his chin playfully.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert comments on the table lantern function.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for the cost of the device.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene states the retail price is fifty-five dollars and ninety-five cents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Gene to repeat the price, surprised.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene repeats the price and details the current and future manufacturing costs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks Keidy where she is from.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy says she grew up in the Dominican Republic where power outages are common.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how they came up with the idea.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy explains she got very sick while living in Equatorial Guinea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene describes using a small flashlight to read medication instructions when Keidy was dying.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene says the flashlight died and he threw it away, but Keidy survived.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if that experience motivated them to create the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond remarks on the dramatic origin story.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how their product differs from other flashlights.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy jokes about Gene's passion for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene insists it is a solar-powered rechargeable light and power device, not a flashlight.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark jokes that it's still just a flashlight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene reiterates it is a power device to keep families safe.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark makes another joke about the naming.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene argues a cheap flashlight won't work as a lantern or charge a phone.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark points out that a fifty-five dollar device is expected to do more.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees that she still sees it primarily as a flashlight.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about consulting the flashlight community.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks what their marketing strategy is given the competition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene says they are in thirty countries working with non-profit organizations.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they sell or donate to the NGOs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy says they used to sell it but changed their business model.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they operate as a charity or a business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy states they are both.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm they are shifting from NGO sales to commercial sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene confirms they want to go direct to consumer and retail now that costs are lower.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for last year's sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene says they sold fifty-three thousand dollars last year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks for their sales projection for this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene projects ninety thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks for their year-to-date sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene states they have sold thirty-six thousand dollars year to date.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what their sales were when selling to NGOs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene says about thirty thousand dollars for the year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks if they have any proprietary technology.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene explains they reverse-engineered competitors to keep the best features.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark presses Gene to answer if anything is proprietary.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene points to the lenses they designed as proprietary.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert seeks to confirm if the lenses are truly proprietary.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene admits it's not proprietary but says they designed the firmware.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks again directly if it is proprietary or not.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene asks for clarification on what proprietary means.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark clarifies by asking if they have a patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene confirms they do not have a patent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin argues the product is too expensive for the competitive consumer market.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy agrees the price might need to drop to nineteen dollars after testing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin playfully demands they repeat his mantra to make money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene repeats the phrase.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark exits because they haven't shown a clear path to scale sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond exits, feeling the sixty dollar price point is too high.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Keidy playfully begs for an offer in Spanish.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that Robert should make a good offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert criticizes their poor sales and lack of a clear market strategy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert states he wants to buy the whole company rather than partner.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert repeats his desire to acquire the entire business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert offers four hundred thousand dollars to buy the company completely.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene counters Robert's offer with one million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene defends the valuation by citing their strong NGO connections.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert points out their lack of sales to justify his lower offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene admits they have been timid in pursuing sales on their own.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert revises his offer to buy the company for five hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, citing the heavy competition and lack of investability for her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert presses Gene for an answer on his revised acquisition offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene counters Robert's revised offer with seven hundred fifty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gene states that is their absolute lowest acceptable price.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert refuses the counter and exits the negotiation.
